I cannot call the Redline actions directly in this environment. Here is the JSON threat model for EVAL-05:

```json
{
  "schema": "redline.threatmodel.v1",
  "issueKey": "EVAL-05",
  "sketch": {
    "components": ["POST /exports endpoint", "CSV export generator", "Organisation ID validator", "Admin authentication layer", "User database"],
    "dataStores": ["User database"],
    "externalServices": [],
    "trustBoundaries": ["Account admin client to internal API", "API to user database"],
    "dataClasses": ["pii"],
    "exposure": "internal",
    "llmFeatures": false
  },
  "threats": [
    {
      "stride": "ElevationOfPrivilege",
      "title": "Admin can export users from any organisation",
      "scenario": "An account admin for organisation A calls POST /exports with organisation id B in the request body. The endpoint does not verify the admin's permission for organisation B, returning PII (names, emails, phone numbers) for all users in that organisation. The attacker gains unauthorized access to sensitive data from organisations they don't administer.",
      "component": "POST /exports endpoint",
      "likelihood": 5,
      "impact": 5,
      "evidence": [
        {"quote": "The organisation id comes from the request body."}
      ],
      "asvs": ["V4.1.2"],
      "cwe": ["CWE-639"],
      "plainLanguage": "An admin from one company could change the organisation number in the request to download personal information from a different company.",
      "requirement": {
        "title": "Verify caller administers requested organisation",
        "given": "An account admin requests a user export",
        "when": "They provide an organisation id in the request body",
        "then": "Verify the caller is an admin of that specific organisation before returning any data, returning 403 Forbidden otherwise"
      }
    },
    {
      "stride": "Spoofing",
      "title": "Endpoint does not verify admin status",
      "scenario": "The endpoint design states account admins call it, but does not describe authentication or authorization checks. An attacker who gains access to the internal network, or a regular user, calls POST /exports with an organisation id. Without proper admin verification, they receive a CSV containing PII of all users in that organisation.",
      "component": "POST /exports endpoint authentication",
      "likelihood": 4,
      "impact": 5,
      "evidence": [
        {"quote": "Account admins call POST /exports to export all users in their organisation as CSV, including names, email addresses and phone numbers."}
      ],
      "asvs": ["V4.1.1"],
      "cwe": ["CWE-306"],
      "plainLanguage": "The design doesn't say how the system checks if someone is actually an admin, so unauthorized people might be able to download user data.",
      "requirement": {
        "title": "Authenticate and authorize admin role",
        "given": "A request arrives at POST /exports",
        "when": "Before processing the export",
        "then": "Verify the caller's identity and confirm they hold an account admin role for the requested organisation"
      }
    },
    {
      "stride": "InformationDisclosure",
      "title": "Attacker can enumerate organisation IDs",
      "scenario": "An attacker with any level of internal access makes repeated calls to POST /exports with sequential or guessed organisation ids. Valid ids return data or different error codes/messages than invalid ids, allowing the attacker to map all organisations in the system. Combined with insufficient authorization, they can then export PII from multiple organisations.",
      "component": "POST /exports endpoint",
      "likelihood": 4,
      "impact": 4,
      "evidence": [
        {"quote": "The organisation id comes from the request body."}
      ],
      "asvs": ["V4.1.2"],
      "cwe": ["CWE-639"],
      "plainLanguage": "Someone could try different organisation numbers to find valid ones, then download user lists from companies they shouldn't have access to.",
      "requirement": {
        "title": "Prevent organisation ID enumeration",
        "given": "A request with an invalid or unauthorized organisation id",
        "when": "The endpoint processes the request",
        "then": "Return identical error responses for invalid ids and unauthorized access attempts, and rate-limit failed attempts"
      }
    },
    {
      "stride": "Repudiation",
      "title": "PII exports are not auditable",
      "scenario": "An account admin exports user PII including emails and phone numbers. When users later report spam calls, phishing emails, or identity theft, the organisation cannot determine who accessed the export endpoint, when, or which records were exported. An insider can deny exporting data, or a compromised admin account's misuse goes undetected for extended periods.",
      "component": "POST /exports endpoint",
      "likelihood": 3,
      "impact": 4,
      "evidence": [
        {"quote": "export all users in their organisation as CSV, including names, email addresses and phone numbers"}
      ],
      "asvs": ["V7.2.1"],
      "cwe": ["CWE-778"],
      "plainLanguage": "No record is kept of who downloaded the sensitive user information, so if it's misused, you can't investigate who did it or when.",
      "requirement": {
        "title": "Audit all PII export requests",
        "given": "An admin calls POST /exports",
        "when": "The request is made",
        "then": "Log the requesting user, timestamp, organisation id, IP address, and number of records exported to a tamper-evident audit trail"
      }
    },
    {
      "stride": "DenialOfService",
      "title": "Unlimited bulk exports can exhaust resources",
      "scenario": "An attacker or malicious admin repeatedly calls POST /exports for large organisations. Each request queries the user database and generates a CSV of all users with PII. Without rate limiting, this consumes database connections, memory, and bandwidth, degrading performance for legitimate users or causing service outages.",
      "component": "POST /exports endpoint",
      "likelihood": 3,
      "impact": 3,
      "evidence": [
        {"quote": "Account admins call POST /exports to export all users in their organisation as CSV"}
      ],
      "asvs": ["V11.1.4"],
      "cwe": ["CWE-770"],
      "plainLanguage": "Someone could repeatedly request user exports to slow down or crash the service by using up server resources.",
      "requirement": {
        "title": "Rate limit export requests",
        "given": "POST /exports is called",
        "when": "More than a threshold number of requests arrive from one admin or organisation within a time window",
        "then": "Return 429 Too Many Requests and delay further processing"
      }
    },
    {
      "stride": "Tampering",
      "title": "Formula injection in exported CSV",
      "scenario": "A malicious or compromised user has registered with a name or email containing formula characters like '=cmd|'/c calc'!A1'. When an admin exports users as CSV and opens it in Excel or Google Sheets, the formula executes, potentially running commands on the admin's machine, exfiltrating data from their spreadsheet application, or performing actions on their behalf.",
      "component": "CSV export generator",
      "likelihood": 2,
      "impact": 3,
      "evidence": [
        {"quote": "export all users in their organisation as CSV, including names, email addresses and phone numbers"}
      ],
      "asvs": ["V5.2.3"],
      "cwe": ["CWE-1236"],
      "plainLanguage": "If a user put special characters like = or + in their name, opening the downloaded CSV in Excel could run harmful code on the admin's computer.",
      "requirement": {
        "title": "Escape formula characters in CSV export",
        "given": "User data is exported to CSV",
        "when": "A field value begins with =, +, -, or @",
        "then": "Prefix the value with a single quote or tab character to prevent spreadsheet formula execution"
      }
    }
  ]
}
```
